c.tagline: Kerala's laid-back capital — the golden Padmanabhaswamy Temple, palm-fringed Kovalam sands, and the gateway to the backwaters.

taxi.fareNote: Autos are metered but drivers often prefer a negotiated fare — agree it first, or book via Uber/Ola for a fixed price. Prepaid taxi counters operate at the airport and Central station.

emergency.note: 112 is India's single all-services emergency number; 108 reaches ambulance services and 100 the police.

avoid.reason: Avoid isolated stretches of Shanghumugham beach after dark and watch belongings in the East Fort market crowds; agree auto-rickshaw fares upfront.

hood_desc: The historic heart around the golden-gopuram Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple, the Kuthira Malika palace and the buzzing Chalai bazaar; the most atmospheric, traditional part of the city and close to the Central railway station.

The central civic and cultural belt along MG Road, taking in the Napier Museum, Sri Chitra Art Gallery, the zoo, the Secretariat and Palayam's mosque-church-temple cluster; the walkable middle of the city.

Kerala's most famous beach resort, 16 km south — a crescent of sand below a candy-striped lighthouse, lined with seafood shacks, Ayurveda spas and hotels from backpacker to five-star. Relaxed and holiday-minded.
The green, modern IT city on the northern edge around Technopark and Kazhakkoottam, with newer hotels, malls and easy airport access; convenient and quiet rather than sightseeing-central.
lodging: The Leela Kovalam, A Raviz Hotel
Uday Samudra Leisure Beach Hotel & Spa

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water and skip ice of unknown origin.

transit.hours: KSRTC and private city buses run roughly 5:30 AM to 10:00 PM; ride apps and autos cover the late-night gap.
transit.note: Thiruvananthapuram has no metro. KSRTC and private buses are the backbone of city transport, with metered and app-booked auto-rickshaws widely available. Tourist boats run the backwaters and lagoons from Kovalam, Poovar and Veli, and beaches line the coast south of the city.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash to the conductor on board. Autos are cash or app; agree an auto fare before you board. There is no rechargeable city transit card.

tip.r: Not customary; rounding up or leaving 5-10% at nicer restaurants and resorts is appreciated but not expected.

landmarks: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple
This gold-plated Dravidian shrine to reclining Vishnu, famed for its vault of unimaginable treasure, dominates the old city with its towering seven-tier gopuram.
Kovalam Beach
Kerala's most celebrated seaside escape, a crescent of golden coves watched over by a striped lighthouse, with surf, seafood shacks and ayurvedic resorts.
Napier Museum and Zoo
A whimsical 19th-century Indo-Saracenic palace of striped brickwork houses bronzes, ivory carvings and Kathakali figures amid gardens shared with one of India's oldest zoos.
Kuthira Malika (Puthen Malika Palace)
The 'Mansion of Horses', a teak-and-granite royal palace beside the temple, dazzles with 122 carved wooden horses, crystal thrones and traditional Travancore craftsmanship.
Shanghumukham Beach
The city's own sunset beach near the airport, famous for its colossal sculpted mermaid, Arattu ritual processions and evening crowds savouring sea breezes.
Attukal Bhagavathy Temple
Known as the Sabarimala of women, this goddess temple hosts the Attukal Pongala, when millions of women cooking offerings form a record-breaking sea of hearths.
Kanakakunnu Palace
A rose-hued hilltop palace of the Travancore maharajas, now a cultural venue whose lawns, sculpture garden and festivals make it a favourite city retreat.
Veli Tourist Village
Where lake meets sea, this leisure park offers pedal boats, a floating bridge and sculptures, capped by artist Jayan's dramatic waterfront installations.
Kowdiar Palace
A former royal residence on the aptly named Royal Road, still home to the Travancore family and visible through its ornate gates.
Connemara Market
A colonial-era covered market near East Fort, its cast-iron arcades sheltering stalls of spices, flowers, and produce since the 19th century.

train.note: No international trains. Thiruvananthapuram Central is the southern end of the Kerala coastal line, with long-distance services north through Kollam, Alleppey and Ernakulam to Mumbai and Delhi and the Kanyakumari trains running south. Book on IRCTC 60 days ahead; the Vande Bharat up the Kerala coast is the fastest option.

bus.note: No international coaches. KSRTC Kerala (https://www.keralartc.com/) runs from the Thampanoor bus station opposite the railway station to Kanyakumari, Kovalam, Varkala and up the coast, with interstate services to Bengaluru and Chennai and private sleepers on redBus (https://www.redbus.in/).

ferry.note: There is no passenger ferry from Thiruvananthapuram; Vizhinjam nearby is a new deep-water container port, not a passenger terminal. Backwater boats operate further north around Kollam and Alleppey.

half.name: Ponmudi
half.blurb: A misty Western Ghats hill station of winding hairpin bends, tea gardens and trekking trails, rising 1,100 metres above the city's tropical heat.

half.name: Poovar Island
half.blurb: Golden sandbanks separate serene backwaters from the Arabian Sea at this estuary paradise, explored by boat past floating cottages and coconut-fringed banks.
